title: What I Would Not Pass On
subtitle: A painful inheritance can be interrupted
sourceCredit: Gina Belafonte · The Moth Radio Hour, “Against the Grain”

shot.title: Three generations

shot.title: A hand intercepts
shot.direction: The mother reaches into the bubble’s path before it reaches her daughter.

illustration.direction: The mother steps between grandmother and child with feet firmly planted and one open hand held across the path of the pointed empty speech-shape, fingers relaxed and elbow naturally bent. shot.direction: She states the boundary firmly, without answering criticism with cruelty.

shot.title: The child peeks around
shot.direction: The child looks around the mirror and studies the adults’ faces.

illustration.direction: The daughter peeks around the safe edge of the mirror toward her mother, one small hand touching the frame and the other held near her own waist. Her lifted brows and uncertain mouth ask whether she is at fault. The mother turns immediately toward her with full attention, her boundary hand now lowered. The grandmother stays in the background at ordinary scale. Do not frame the child as guilty or leave her frightened beneath a giant adult hand.

shot.direction: Her question is small; hold enough room for an immediate caring response.

beats.caption: No. You get to be yourself.
beats.speaker: MOTHER

shot.title: You get to be yourself
shot.direction: The mother lowers to the child’s eye line. Her face and hands communicate safety.
shot.soundDirection: Glass chime, paper bubble folding, then a calm indoor ambience.

illustration.direction: The mother crouches naturally to the daughter's eye level, one knee bent and balanced on a real foot, both hands open low near her own knees. She gives the child a clear warm face; the daughter begins to release her grip on the mirror and look back. The grandmother is present at a respectful distance, not banished or monstrous. The pointed speech-shape has stopped beside the mother and cannot reach the girl. No idealized beauty image appears in the mirror.

shot.title: The words laid down
shot.direction: The old critical bubble is placed harmlessly on the table; it is not passed onward.
shot.soundDirection: Glass chime, paper bubble folding, then a calm indoor ambience.

illustration.direction: The mother stands beside the table and sets a small folded dark paper-like speech-shape flat on its surface, wrist and fingertips touching it in one coherent gentle action. The pointed edge no longer aims at anyone. The daughter stands freely beside the mirror with hands relaxed and a small secure expression. The grandmother watches in thoughtful silence from the other side. Their ordinary clothes and the room remain unchanged; the visual metaphor is contained, not weaponized.

shot.title: Later care
shot.direction: A restrained dissolve brings later care for an aging mother; the boundary stays visible.
shot.soundDirection: Glass chime, paper bubble folding, then a calm indoor ambience.

illustration.direction: A restrained later scene in a quieter corner of a domestic room: the same grandmother, visibly older but recognizable, sits firmly in a supportive chair. The mother stands beside her offering one hand for balance, their actual palms meeting naturally. Her other hand is a small open boundary gesture near her own waist, her face gentle and firm. Keep the folded dark shape set aside on a distant table. No child substitute, no diagnosis, no implied forgiveness that erases the boundary.

beats.caption: I can help you, Mom. But not with those words.
beats.speaker: MOTHER
